steps.content: After the promise was made, the suffocating tension dissolved completely. Jasmine has clung to you at almost every waking moment since. It's been a gentle, peaceful stretch of time, much like now.
[Bureau]

A captivating scent fills your office. There on the coffee table, in a shallow dish, sits a freshly made meal. The beef is braised to a melting tenderness, its rich sauce catching the light with a tantalizing sheen.
Jasmine is helpless against the temptation. Without a glance at the cutlery nearby, she reaches out and carefully plucks a piece, holding it up to her mouth.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Ahm—mm...! Hot, hot, hot!

She springs to her feet from the heat, both hands waving wildly to fan her mouth. She refuses to spit the meat out, so she just blows out quick, desperate breaths instead. They say a cat's tongue can't handle anything hot, and Jasmine appears to be no different.

options: Why not let it cool down a bit first?

choices.text: Why not let it cool down a bit first?

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: But then it won't taste the same. I've never had anything this good out there, you know. Whatever I caught myself was always raw, and whatever the desert bandits gave me was always cold. Hot like this... that's where the real flavor is.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Oh, won't you have a bite too, Chief? Here, I'll cool it off for you. Give it a try!
Using both knife and fork, she stabs a piece and bounds over to you. She blows on it carefully, several gentle puffs to cool it, then presents it to your lips with a beaming smile.

This is what your days have become. She's like a changed person, sweet-natured and eager to please. Even when her actions are plainly meant to curry favor, that innocent smile makes them disarming, utterly irresistible.

More astonishing still is that even beyond your sight, she's shed the violence of her past, no longer so quick to react. She's even begun to willingly reach out to people besides you—Disians, of all people.
[Scene Change] Flashback Filter

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: Chief, Chief! You have to hear this! I was delivering files around the departments today, and Jasmine followed me the whole time! Looking around, peeking at everything, it was the cutest thing. She's exactly like my cat. She even rubbed her cheek against my hand! Like this little nuzzle for attention!

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: Oh, I've totally figured out what snacks she loves by now. Next time I'm bringing a whole bag! Hm... where should I take her wandering next?
[Scene Change] Flashback Filter

steps.speaker: Eugene
steps.content: The day before yesterday, she slipped into the crawlspace above the garage maintenance room. How on earth did a fully grown woman climb that high and fold herself into a space that tight?

steps.speaker: Eugene
steps.content: And the creepier part is... she stayed up there the whole day, dead silent. No one had any idea. Then, some guy on night shift happened to glance up, and two glowing eyes blinked right back at him. Now the Bureau's got another ghost story...
[Scene Change] Flashback Filter

steps.speaker: Nurse
steps.content: Look, I know she's doing a lot better now... but she can't just go tearing off wherever she feels like it! Those regular checkups still need to happen! She's way too fast. I can't even catch her! Chief, can you please do something...
[Scene Change] Flashback Filter

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: Hmm... Her aggressive tendencies have vanished entirely. She's more willing to communicate, shows better self-regulation... I have to admit, this far exceeds anything I expected. It's genuinely striking. As a case study, I'd love to dig deeper...

steps.speaker: Doctor
steps.content: ...Chief. You didn't do something, did you? Have your shackles evolved further? Why not accompany her back to Banyan sometime? We'd be happy to provide a full examination, on the house...
[Door Opens] Back to Present

It's a good thing. You've always wished she could feel the kindness of more people, could open her eyes and truly see those around her once again. And Jasmine, as though she understood your unspoken hopes, has done exactly that.

One by one, the "promises" are being kept. Even when your work piles up and keeps you, even when your thoughts are elsewhere weaving other plans, she never urges you, never stirs up a fuss. She simply stays at your side with a smile, gazing at you.
Still, that taut string hidden deep in your heart refuses to loosen.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief, here's the report from the Outland Affairs Bureau. There's been an update on those desert bandits you asked us to track.

You page through the file. Jasmine had passed through the hands of several bandit crews back then. All of them had been questioned, and all of them had come clean about how they stumbled on her, tricked her, used her as a weapon against sand beasts and competing gangs. Now and then, they'd feed her a few DisCity sheriffs to toy with, as a prize.

But the promises were never real. DisCity was never the destination. And no one could speak to her past: where she had come from, whether she still had family, what had hollowed her out into this. The bandits had never bothered to learn.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...That's all there is?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: I'm afraid so. The Ash Campaign hit the bandit groups hard as well. Those who had direct contact with Jasmine back then are nearly impossible to find now.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: And in any case, the bandits only valued her combat strength. To them, she was just a mentally unstable refugee from the Outlands, someone easy to string along... They never cared what she'd gone through, so they can't offer any useful information. As for the rest...
She pauses, following your gaze toward the corner.

In the corner of the office, Jasmine is perched silently on the coffee table. She watches the two of you, perfectly still except for her hand, which inches the glass before her ever closer to the edge, a fraction at a time. By now, it teeters at the table's rim, a sliver of it already suspended over nothing.
The instant she catches your gaze, her hand retreats. She looks up at you with big, dewy eyes, the very picture of blamelessness.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: ...Chief, Jasmine really has come a long way. Perhaps you can let yourself ease up a little. You don't have to carry so much tension.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Just leave the files here. I'll go through them more carefully in a bit. If any new leads surface, I'll need you to follow up on them again.
Nightingale sighs. In the end, she says nothing more, only setting the files down on your desk in silence.
The moment she exits the room, Jasmine springs to your side.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Hehe, desert bandits are so dull... Didn't the adjutant lady bring anything else?
You know exactly what she wants to hear.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The report says the Shattered Blade's mission is still ongoing. You know how it is out there, Apostles crawling everywhere, disasters at every turn. These things take time.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: We'll wait together. If you're getting bored, how about you tell me some stories? About the world out there?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Where you've been, who you've crossed paths with, how long you spent in each place, anything strange or wonderful that happened... Whatever you can recall, I want to hear all of it.
Jasmine studies you for a long moment, and an impish smile spreads across her lips.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Mm... I don't really remember. Nothing worth talking about anyway. Oh! I hear Wynn out there! Gonna go play with her!

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: You're busy anyway. I'll do what you want and go meet more of my "friends."

She leans back, rolls away from your grasp, and bolts out the door quick as a fox. Moments later, peals of happy laughter echo from outside. It's Wynn and some other staff members, their voices warm with affection. Everyone adores Jasmine, cares for her, believes in her, overjoyed by her "recovery."
—Only you know the truth.
[Switch Scene]
Each night, you let Jasmine have the bed while you lie on the sofa nearby. In the deep hours of the night, her painful moans reach you again.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Nn... nngh... Stay away... no!
You turn to her at once and take her hand in yours.

options: Jasmine! Wake up! I'm right here!

choices.text: Jasmine! Wake up! I'm right here!

steps.content: Her eyes snap open, and she shoots upright in the dark. Her pupils, wide and shaking, are fixed on some nightmare beyond your sight. Sweat-soaked but deathly chill, she pants, and those rapid, broken breaths cut through the dead quiet, squeezing your heart tight.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Jasmine, it's just me. You had another nightmare. Are you okay? Should I call the doctor?

You lift a hand to wipe away her sweat, only to startle her. Jasmine jerks away, scrambling back against the wall, hands fumbling frantically in the corner. You know all too well what she's reaching for. Those savage blades.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Your blades aren't here. This isn't the battlefield. You don't need weapons here.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The nightmare's over, Jasmine.
She gazes at you for a long while. When you finally lower your hand, still poised awkwardly in mid-reach, she softens just slightly, returning to the present. A dry chuckle escapes her.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: ...I'm fine, Chief. It wasn't a nightmare... It was a sweet dream...

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: I dreamed I was back at the celebration. I was dancing, seeing everyone I wanted to see. All of them...
[Flashback: Small CG - Burning Village]

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Heh... such a sweet dream... You shouldn't have woken me. That's where I'm supposed to be...
She curls into herself, arms wrapped tight around her body, her laughter dwindling into near silence.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Jasmine, that's...

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Go back to sleep, Chief. I'll sleep too... The celebration's still waiting for me... in my dreams...

She bundles the bedding and climbs off the bed, steering clear of you. She weaves drowsily around the tables and chairs that belong to Disians, drifting like a sleepwalker, until she sinks into a cold corner of the room. The blanket goes over her head. She shrinks into a tiny, shadowed knot.
You can only watch.
You cannot bear to leave, but you cannot move closer. This is the fractured reality that tears between you. In waking life, the chasm filled with pain is impassable. But at least in dreams, it isn't.

Now you can join her in those nightmares. They are so vivid now. The moment your eyes close, you are back on that battlefield you fought so hard to forget. The vast spiral, the blood spilled, the hatred swallowed. Yours and not yours alike, they coil around you, grinding everything to dust beneath your feet.
So you try to abandon sleep. It brings its own rewards: by day, you can focus your mind on tracing Jasmine's past. By night, you can keep watch and pull her back from the nightmares in time.

Time is slipping away. You must find answers. You must carve out a path for her before a darker ending arrives. You have to go deeper into her past, sifting through shattered, chaotic memories for any fragment of possibility.
After countless dead ends, you finally find a crack.
—It's a call coming in from Nirvana Port.
[Switch Scene]

steps.speaker: Iron-Masked Man
steps.content: We finished analyzing that pair of Rancor blades you sent over. They've been reforged, with heavy damage across both, but the material composition, manufacturing batch, and Mania signature all left traces. Enough to make a match.

steps.speaker: Iron-Masked Man
steps.content: They belonged to the last batch of Rancors, manufactured N.F. 92. Issued in stages to six battalions. Three of those were later deployed to different overseas bases. All three went silent starting N.F. 102.

steps.speaker: Iron-Masked Man
steps.content: Cross-reference with that woman's age, and it lines up with the RNH Battalion. They fought through the one-year war after BR-003, from N.F. 106 to 107.

steps.speaker: Iron-Masked Man
steps.content: Without central command from DisCity, the RNH wandered. Scavenged their own supplies, fought their own battles. They covered too much ground and passed through countless settlements. Hard to pin down an exact location.

steps.speaker: Iron-Masked Man
steps.content: Report's in your hands now. If you want to help her find her roots, go do it yourself.
The report is thorough. It sets out a clear perimeter within the blighted wasteland and pinpoints several sites of interest. This could be enough to lead you to Jasmine's homeland.
You should thank him, but your instinct pulls another question from your lips.

options: ...Is the RNH Battalion still with the Shattered Blade?

choices.text: ...Is the RNH Battalion still with the Shattered Blade?

steps.speaker: Iron-Masked Man
steps.content: No. Their gear was already obsolete the year they deployed. And during their time fighting alone out there, losses were catastrophic. By the time Augustus pulled them back, there wasn't much left to salvage. The battalion was disbanded and merged shortly after.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I meant the soldiers under its command. The ones who survived. Any of them still out there? Where are they now?

options: I want to talk to them.

choices.text: I want to talk to them.

steps.content: The line goes stiff with silence. When Iron Mask finally speaks again, his voice has dropped, low and grim.

steps.speaker: Iron-Masked Man
steps.content: The support you asked for, we already gave it. Whether we should have or not, the Shattered Blade delivered. What's left... you can't reckon with, and you can't collect. This stops now.

steps.speaker: Iron-Masked Man
steps.content: If you still want to do something for that Outland woman, sort it out inside your own Bureau.
You try to keep him on the line, but a commotion of some sort has broken out on his side.

steps.speaker: Iron-Masked Man
steps.content: ...Go back. This doesn't involve you.
Those words are not meant for you. You can tell Iron Mask has stepped back from the microphone. Beyond him, another voice reaches you, distant and unclear.
Someone else is there, imploring Iron Mask about something, and they refuse to be dismissed.

steps.speaker: Iron-Masked Man
steps.content: Ten minutes. And this stays sealed between the two of you only. Clear?

A few more muffled words come through. Then you hear the receiver being set down, two sets of heavy footfalls crossing, one retreating and the other approaching. Someone else reaches the communicator and lifts the receiver.
A stranger's voice greets you, gravelly and strained.

Chief of the Minos Bureau of Crisis Control. My name is Arkin, Logistics Task Force, Shattered Blade. Before we came back to Nirvana Port, I was with the RNH Battalion, one of the old DisCorps overseas units.

steps.speaker: Arkin
steps.content: I'm grateful you'd even ask about my old unit. Whatever you need to know about the RNH Battalion... if I remember it, it's yours.

options: ...Walk me through every combat operation RNH ever carried out.

choices.text: ...Walk me through every combat operation RNH ever carried out.

steps.content: After a long, deep breath, Arkin answers your question.

N.F. 106, the year of the Great Expo. Under the cover of "peace," a small faction of Outlanders colluded with the Underground and detonated BR-003. From that flashpoint, a new city-state war ignited, and the news tore across thousands of miles to reach the RNH Battalion.

It wasn't because DisCity's communications were working. They'd been severed from the homeland for years. But that didn't slow the war's spread.
Almost the same time the conflict erupted, the RNH camp came under assault. Unlike the abandoned soldiers of DisCity, the Outlands had been preparing for total war from the start. The pretext they broadcast for mobilization was that "DisCity deliberately triggered BR-003, unleashing disasters and seeking to wield Mania to once again dominate and exploit the farlands."

The ranks of the RNH Battalion were filled with the young, men and women in their twenties and thirties. A great many had endured the BR-001 disaster in N.F. 89. After joining the military, they only understood more clearly the true cost it had demanded. They knew DisCity could not survive a Black Ring. The lie filled them with fury. "DisCity could never detonate a Black Ring. We're the ones who bore its real cost. You twist the truth. You're the criminals here!" "What's become of the city... the Black Ring, the Mania... what the hell have you bastards done?! Where's my mom? How's everyone...? I want to go home. I want to go home..." "...How DARE you?! Outland filth. You will PAY for this!!"

Stoked by hatred, the war sank swiftly into a blood-soaked stalemate.
Every settlement in view was manufacturing guns and bullets. The enemy hid war criminals inside civilian hospitals, sent the elderly, the frail women and children out to the roadsides swathed in bandages, pleading for rescue. When DisCity soldiers approached, the bombs sewn into their cloaks would ignite without warning. That was how Arkin lost his leg, the same death trap that took his comrades.

This stray remnant force refused to surrender. If DisCity ever mounted a counteroffensive, their position would also serve as a critical passage. They believed their homeland's main force might still come. The RNH Battalion resisted with their Rancors, sustaining themselves on the spoils of battle, down to the very last soldier.
...Until every threat in the region was at last annihilated.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...So you're telling me everything RNH swept through were military targets? Hidden in villages, in towns?

steps.speaker: Arkin
steps.content: I'm certain of it.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: And the civilians? All of them are enemy combatants in disguise, waiting to strike?

steps.speaker: Arkin
steps.content: Everyone in RNH died that way. Every last one except me.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...But you said RNH was short-handed, cut off from command. What intel were you operating on? How did you make those calls? And what if you got it wrong?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Did you expect the Rancors in your hands to tell you who to kill and who to spare?
Bang!

A metal fist slams hard against a desk on the other end of the line, cutting the conversation short for a moment. Mentioning the past has easily reignited his long-buried hatred. You can feel the fury rolling off him through his breath alone.
When Arkin speaks again, he has barely wrestled his emotions back under control. His voice has grown even rougher.

steps.speaker: Arkin
steps.content: ...We've seen too many cunning, vicious Outlanders. Their "clever little tricks" got far too many of our people killed. That woman may act tame around you...

steps.speaker: Arkin
steps.content: But she's holding a Rancor weapon in her hands, blades she took off our fallen comrades... She even set her sights on General Augustus. That... I can't let that stand.

steps.speaker: Arkin
steps.content: You earned our trust and respect in the Ash Campaign, Chief. From the General to the adjutant, the Shattered Blade considers you one of us.

steps.speaker: Arkin
steps.content: ...I'd hate to see all that thrown away over some Outland Sinner with a questionable background.
There is no pretense in his words. They carry a warning, but even more than that, a plea. This veteran is earnestly begging you not to cross that line, not to side with the "enemy."
...<color=#fb9259>Enemy</color>. That word again. Like the unrelenting nightmares of recent nights, it sends a fresh spasm twisting through your stomach. You hold it down.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...I reached you precisely because I want to settle her "questionable background."

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: She's lost her memory. Mania destroyed her mind completely. I had to use EDGE's technology just to reach her subconscious. And there, I found some clues. Strange ones. They might connect to her past. I need to know if any of it means something to you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Deep in her subconscious, I saw a village on fire. A celebration that never ends. And a song, from the Outlands.
[CG: Burning Village, Screen Dims]
Let flame ignite the candles bright, not scorch the seedlings in the light.
Let arrows fly to strike the mark, not pierce a grandmother's tender heart.
Let parades roll through fields so wide, yet never steal dreams from inside. Let fireworks gleam in skies above, but never burn the homes of love.
O traveler, when you join a celebration in a foreign land... leave blades of slaughter behind.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You've been there. How much do you remember? What happened at <color=#fb9259>that woman's</color> village? At that celebration?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Was it the same as what you told me? Just another filthy military outpost, fake civilians, a staged celebration, all of it a trap meant to kill you?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Answer me.

steps.speaker: Arkin
steps.content: Urgh... bleurgh!!

The only reply is a fit of harsh, convulsive vomiting. The handset on the other end tumbles to the floor as the man goes down. The retching drags on for a long while, tangled with weeping, until someone hauls him off. When the receiver is picked up again, it's Iron Mask who speaks.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: He was there. He knows what he did. Bring him back. If he has a shred of conscience left, he'll face me and answer for it!

steps.speaker: Iron-Masked Man
steps.content: Ten minutes are up, Chief. That was the last exception I'll make for you. This ends here. Goodbye.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You know he's guilty! Are you shielding him from me? Or are you no different from that guy yourself?

steps.speaker: Iron-Masked Man
steps.content: My duty is to keep the Shattered Blade in line. Not to play the saint for you.
[Transition, visual effect, sound effects: crushing sound, sharp static]

A sharp burst of static cuts your question short. The receiver has been crushed. Through the crackling noise, you can barely make out Iron Mask's breathing. It's tight, strained, muffled behind the metal slits of his mask.

steps.speaker: Iron-Masked Man
steps.content: ...The General left DisCity in N.F. 103. While those fools triggered the Black Ring and dragged everyone into war, she was still out there, crossing the lands, weathering the Mania storms, searching for the soldiers they abandoned.

steps.speaker: Iron-Masked Man
steps.content: Even merchants know when to steer clear of danger. Augustus never took a detour in her life. From Eastia to the farlands, she'd go dark for weeks, for months. And you're asking if she knew about that ugly war? Hah.

steps.speaker: Iron-Masked Man
steps.content: If she'd been there, it wouldn't have ended like this. The Black Ring would never have erupted. The year-long war would've been finished in a single day. Those shameless Outlanders wouldn't have dared lift a finger in the first place. Don't you think so?!
Rage, loathing, disdain, and another deep feeling beyond any outsider's reach. Together, they catch fire inside this soldier, rigid and unyielding as forged steel.

steps.speaker: Iron-Masked Man
steps.content: Listen, Chief of Minos. I don't fulfill your requests to earn your goodwill. Not out of guilt toward anyone. Not to shield anyone either.

steps.speaker: Iron-Masked Man
steps.content: We at the DisCorps claimed our seats in hell a long time ago. Your judgment means nothing to us. I help you only because the General saw something in you, nothing more.

steps.speaker: Iron-Masked Man
steps.content: You want to study Rancors? Play your little hero game inside your own Bureau? Do as you like. I can work with that.

steps.speaker: Iron-Masked Man
steps.content: But leave Augustus out of it. And stay out of her way.

steps.speaker: Iron-Masked Man
steps.content: Whether it's the DisCorps or that Outland woman, the moment they took up a Rancor, they became something different from you. You still have the sense to keep your distance from war. You'll never understand what those weapons really mean.

steps.speaker: Iron-Masked Man
steps.content: If you insist on interfering, on fighting for that Outlander's justice... then by all means. Bring her to <color=#fb9259>Nirvana Port</color>. Make it soon. I'll be here.
He lets out a cold laugh.

steps.speaker: Iron-Masked Man
steps.content: I'm curious to see... how you'll handle the consequences when that day comes.
The dead silence freezes time itself. It drags on, and on, until you grow weary of this standoff. You no longer know what meaning there could be in repeating this same confrontation.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Jasmine isn't a "Rancor." She doesn't belong on a battlefield. She's nothing like you people.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'm returning her blades to the Shattered Blade. They'll be delivered immediately. Take them and go. As far from here as you can get.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: And don't ever come near her again.

steps.speaker: Iron-Masked Man
steps.content: A sound decision. I'll be waiting for your update.
[Scene Change: Chief's Room, Late Night]
That night, ${PlayerName} comes back very late.
Finding Jasmine already lying down and deep in sleep, he returns to the "sofa" beside her, his glowing tablet in hand, and taps away at it long into the quiet.
steps.female_content: Finding Jasmine already lying down and deep in sleep, she returns to the "sofa" beside her, her glowing tablet in hand, and taps away at it long into the quiet.

steps.content: When the sounds from across the room at last stop and the glow goes out, Jasmine, in the darkness, opens her eyes.

${PlayerName} has fallen asleep, head drooping. She rises, steps on tiptoe across the cold tiles, and creeps noiselessly to his side. Imitating the way ${PlayerName} always does it, she taps at the machine still resting in his hands.
steps.female_content: ${PlayerName} has fallen asleep, head drooping. She rises, steps on tiptoe across the cold tiles, and creeps noiselessly to her side. Imitating the way ${PlayerName} always does it, she taps at the machine still resting in her hands.

steps.content: The screen lights up again. She sees several little squares: some photographs, some strange drawings. She peers closer—
She can't make sense of it. It's a jumbled mess to her.

She is about to keep browsing when a soft noise stops her cold. She jolts and skips back a step. ${PlayerName} stirs faintly, brows knitting together, and a few indistinct words fall from those lips. But in the end, the Chief stays asleep.
How rare. All this time, he's never once taken his eyes off Jasmine. Has so many sleepless days finally caught up with him? Is he dreaming right now?
steps.female_content: How rare. All this time, she's never once taken her eyes off Jasmine. Has so many sleepless days finally caught up with her? Is she dreaming right now?

steps.content: That only makes it better. Jasmine slips close again—

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: What's troubling you, Chief?

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: If you can't sleep, I'll stay right here with you.

Another few indistinct murmurs escape ${PlayerName}. Jasmine presses closer still, ghosting her fingertips along the cheek and earlobe. She let her words drift into the Chief's ear like a breath, threading them into those dreams, coaxing answers out:

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: You were gone alone for so long today... Did the Shattered Blade come back?

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Is my wish going to come true soon?

${PlayerName}'s eyes snap open with a violent start. A hand pushes Jasmine away, palm blazing, glowing with the threat of something ominous about to break loose. Jasmine feels a spike of primal fear, her body poised to bolt.

But just before the force can fully unleash, his eyes focus, and he sees her. The moment he registers it's Jasmine, his expression shifts into something even more terrified than before. He wrenches his hand back as if electrocuted, scrambling backward to put space between them. His voice emerges ragged and shaking.
steps.female_content: But just before the force can fully unleash, her eyes focus, and she sees her. The moment she registers it's Jasmine, her expression shifts into something even more terrified than before. She wrenches her hand back as if electrocuted, scrambling backward to put space between them. Her voice emerges ragged and shaking.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Sorry, Jasmine... I was dreaming. I didn't realize it was you...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Sorry... that was my fault. I'm sorry...

${PlayerName} tries to stand but collapses back onto the sofa, his hand coming up to cover his face. His breathing is harsh and unsteady. The terminal hits the floor and glows to life again. By its light, Jasmine sees it now: his lips are frighteningly pale, cold sweat soaking his brow, the frantic hammer of his heart almost audible.
steps.female_content: ${PlayerName} tries to stand but collapses back onto the sofa, her hand coming up to cover her face. Her breathing is harsh and unsteady. The terminal hits the floor and glows to life again. By its light, Jasmine sees it now: her lips are frighteningly pale, cold sweat soaking her brow, the frantic hammer of her heart almost audible.

steps.content: He's lost weight. Jasmine's never seen him like this, with his eyes hollowed out and bloodshot. How many nights has it been since he last slept well? After every smile he gave her, every gentle moment... was his face always like this beneath it all?
steps.female_content: She's lost weight. Jasmine's never seen her like this, with her eyes hollowed out and bloodshot. How many nights has it been since she last slept well? After every smile she gave her, every gentle moment... was her face always like this beneath it all?

steps.content: Jasmine knows what hatred feels like. She remembers love and longs for it. But this expression is something she's never witnessed before. She freezes in place. A long silence passes before her body stirs. Without realizing it, she steps forward and slowly, gently wraps her arms around the person before her.
${PlayerName}'s body tenses for a moment.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: It's okay, it's okay... You still have Jasmine. I'm here with you...
She strokes the Chief's back in slow, gentle beats, easing the chaotic heaving of that chest little by little.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Tomorrow... I think it's supposed to be sunny...

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: We could go outside. Maybe... you could come with me, Chief?

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: I've explored every corner of the Bureau already, but I don't know what's fun out there yet. Maybe... you could pick a few places?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...What do you want to do, Jasmine?

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: I'm not clever enough to think of anything. You tell me, Chief.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Spring is almost here. The sunlight will be beautiful. By then... there might be performances in the city. All kinds of them...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: There'll be music, lights, good food, and shows... People from everywhere, dressed up in pretty clothes, singing and dancing together. Like a celebration.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Hehe. Wynn told you about that, didn't she? It all sounds lovely. I'd love every bit of it. And since it's what you want, how about we go see them all?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Of course. I just want you to be happy.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: As long as you can be happy...
The smile slips from Jasmine's face. She gazes at you for a long while before her voice finally comes.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: ...Why are you crying, Chief?
Are you crying?

No. It's just the remnants of that nightmare. Iron and blood. Fire and ash. Blistering heat and the stink of rot. You hear the roars and the wails. Sacrifice and hatred churning together, stirred up again and again with vicious intent, bleeding outward until they solidify into a vast, oppressive spiral.

That's nothing but a dream, the aftermath of your brief time at war and the suffering others described. But your soul, the ones and the things you truly hold dear, none of them were ever swallowed by that war.
You are lucky. You took everything back just in time, so you still had the chance to escape the battlefield. To run far, far from it all.
But what about them?

steps.speaker: Iron-Masked Man
steps.content: Whether it's the DisCorps or that Outland woman, the moment they took up a Rancor, they became something different from you. You still have the sense to keep your distance from war. You'll never understand what those weapons really mean.

He was right. You don't know how to do right by Jasmine, don't know what you can get back for her, don't know how to bring her away from all this. Your face is dry, your eyes dry. You haven't cried. It's not your turn yet.
But Jasmine reaches up anyway and brushes her fingers across your cheek. For the first time, those luminous, fawn-like eyes of hers cloud over with a haze you cannot quite see through.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: ...You shouldn't cry for me. The times I lashed out, the nightmares, all the lying, running off, picking fights... I did all those terrible things, but none of that was ever your fault. I don't hate you. I never did.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: I know you're such a good person. You're the kindest. If anyone should be sorry, it's me...

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: I'm sorry, Chief. I lied to you, I used you, I never listened. I took your kindness and threw it back at you. And I made you so, so sad.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: But... I really do like you. I always have. Your love isn't something worthless. It's the best thing anyone's ever given me.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: I don't know what happiness really is. But if you see it as so precious, then I want you to have every last bit of it. So please, don't cry. Smile for me, okay?

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: I love seeing people smile the most...
You force out a smile and draw her in your arms, burying the look that follows.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Promise me one thing, Jasmine. Whatever you choose to do, wherever you go, whatever happens, let me stay beside you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I won't get in your way... I have no right to ask you to let go. And I can't pretend I can ever make up for everything you've lost.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But if there's something, out beyond your celebration, here in the waking world... if there's anything still worth holding onto, even a little... tell me.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Even if it's just the faintest hope, as long as you're willing... I want you to be happy.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Sleep now, Chief... Tonight, I will watch over you. Sleep. Have a sweet dream...
As you feel the rhythm of her breath and the beat of her heart, exhaustion and drowsiness, held at bay for so long, finally wash over you like a tide.
You fall into another dream.

In the dream, the bloodstained blades are sent out of the Bureau on schedule. You watch as they're locked into a suppressant casing and placed inside an armored transport. Past the port checkpoint, through the sandstorm, they'll finally return to the place they were always meant to be.
And Jasmine accepts it calmly. She lets go of the inseparable blades just like that, shedding nine years of fixation. She doesn't even bother to look again.
She stays beside you. She tells you not to worry. She's right there when you fall asleep, just like tonight.
...Tonight, she watches you as you drift deep into sleep. She sees your brow smooth out at last and thinks to herself—maybe, just maybe, you're finally having a good dream.
Jasmine reaches toward you, but pulls her hand back before it can land.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: It's enough if you are happy... Your love is precious.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: From now on... save more of it for yourself...

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: I'm sorry...

Three days after the Rancor blades were sent away from the MBCC,
Sinner Jasmine fled the Bureau. Her absence went undetected for two whole hours. Not a single alarm was raised.

Passwords, monitoring gaps, security zones, corridor schedules, patrol movements, even the psychological vulnerabilities of every staff member she interacted with... This "pitiful patient," supposedly "mentally broken" and "cognitively degraded," had quietly mastered it all, then leveraged every piece of it with surgical cunning.

Her final choice was the medical waste collection vehicle. She hid herself within its contamination isolation chamber and escaped. The timing was immaculate.

She had stockpiled her own prescribed sedatives, dissolved them into your tea, and left while you slept soundly. She knew precisely when you would finally let your guard down.
The entire Bureau was thrown into shock.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: So... all that time Jasmine spent following me around... it was just to get out? Is she going after the Shattered Blade by herself? What's going to happen to her?

steps.speaker: Eugene
steps.content: Hold on. No matter how well she plays it, her Mania sensitivity readings are off the charts. The second she steps into WhiteSands, the Ash Apostles' fields will scramble her sense of direction completely. She won't be able to find her way. She knows that. She knows she can't reach the Shattered Blade alone.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...She knows. She's known all along.
So she planned it all from the start...

Your knuckles whiten, cold sweat sliding down your skin as your gaze stays locked on the external comms. One channel has been silent. Too silent, for too long. Nightingale reads the implication before anyone else does.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: ...The transport carrying those Rancor blades was headed for Nirvana Port.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: It underwent final inspections at the port last night before departure. They flagged a medium-risk anomaly, which held it up for three hours. Did she slip in during that window? Or did she... cause that delay herself...

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief!
[Scene Change]
She crawls out of the upturned transport and staggers blindly into the WhiteSands. The wind flays her skin; the Apostles' thunderous roars scramble her mind, turning every direction into nothing.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Here in the waking world... if there's anything still worth holding onto, even a little... tell me.
There is... there is. Everything you gave me. Thank you for being so kind to me. For giving me so much.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Whatever you choose to do, wherever you go, whatever happens, let me stay beside you.
I'm sorry. I never learned how to hold onto anything good. I hope... it won't hurt too much.
The celebration isn't over. I have to go back. I have to...

She's close now. So close. The Rancor, clutched tight for nine long years, finds its way back into her hands. It feels its companions somewhere near. The blades will show the way, leading the wandering dancer across seas of spilled blood, through the long years, back to the stage she never truly left.
This time, she will not dance alone. She can feel it—
Up ahead, <color=#fb9259>familiar faces</color> from that year already stand waiting on the stage, ready to join her and complete the celebration that never ended.

At Nirvana Port, the watch has changed shifts. Arkin stands guard over the shipping lane toward DisCity, but all he sees is a sea of fire. That phone call was just the cure his peace needed; it stripped away every last shred of it, and now every nightmare has awakened again.

steps.speaker: Arkin
steps.content: ..."Leave blades of slaughter behind"... Heh... That's not how they used to sing it...
The rust-coated Rancor rifle trembles in his grip. Mania leaks free. Behind him, soldiers are falling in, all brothers-in-arms bound by the same shared nightmare.
Now that same irresistible scent reaches them all: the gore of a past massacre, an invitation no battlefield specter can ever refuse.

steps.speaker: Arkin
steps.content: ...Yes. You're right.

steps.speaker: Arkin
steps.content: ...Following orders is a soldier's sacred duty. Eliminating the enemy is all that matters.

steps.speaker: Arkin
steps.content: Everything you said... it's all true... but...
He looks toward the distance, and a smile creeps onto his lips unbidden.

steps.speaker: Arkin
steps.content: Look... She's here.
The shadow of Nirvana Port reaches outward, like some waking creature, like a long runner rolled out to greet a guest.

Before it, a thin figure approaches, unsteady on her feet. She seems so small, and yet so achingly familiar. It is as though this long-dormant grave has been waiting for her alone, waiting to be stirred back to life.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: I'm finally out... Heheh... This is right. I'm back...

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: ...Now, let the celebration begin...
She raises her Rancor. They all raise theirs. The long-lost weapon has at last returned to the place it has yearned for day and night. And after all this time, she feels a true heartbeat at last.
At that time, you don't yet understand. The deeper a Rancor is pulled into the battlefield, the less meaning attachment and possession can ever hold.
Only through taking can their hearts be awakened.
